C-BROWSER-REQUEST-POLICY-INTERCEPTION-SC.Summary:
This superseding bundle is limited to the authorized scope correction for the predecessor C-BROWSER-REQUEST-POLICY-INTERCEPTION-20260902. It keeps the implementation, architecture, acceptance criteria and verification intent unchanged while making the three already-used evidence/helper files explicit in the replacement plan's ObservedWriteScope.
Deliver the next bounded M1.3 browser-service slice by introducing an explicit, deadline-bounded request interception path and proving it with a replaceable ad-blocking policy plugin against the real CEF provider.
The primary product of this change is not a new ad-blocking ecosystem or a proprietary filter language. The primary product is a generic Worldline mechanism by which an authorized policy plugin can inspect bounded network request metadata before dispatch and return an explicit allow/block decision without turning the event bus into RPC or embedding policy in CEF.
A minimal deterministic adblock policy is the first proving consumer. More capable providers, including providers that reuse established filtering engines or rule formats, remain replaceable follow-on implementations behind the same request-policy boundary.
C-BROWSER-REQUEST-POLICY-INTERCEPTION-SC.Problem:
The predecessor plan was approved and executed, but its observed-write scope omitted three files that are part of the same implementation state: the T-004 feasibility harness, the parallel-safe real-CEF lock helper, and the synchronization-only S3B touch.
M1.2 and the completed M1.3 service slices provide a real CEF engine provider, browser service plugins, durable downloads and cookies/site-data, but they do not yet provide a network-time policy interception mechanism.
Existing browser events report facts after or around browser activity. They cannot answer the synchronous question that request filtering requires: whether a concrete outgoing request should be allowed to continue before it reaches the network.
Implementing ad blocking directly inside `worldline-browser-cef` would make CEF own product policy, couple the browser engine to one filtering strategy, and make future privacy, enterprise or other request policies engine-specific.
Implementing the decision through the event bus would violate the project invariant that EVENT BUS IS NOT RPC and would create unbounded latency, ordering and failure ambiguity on a hot network path.
A separate interception boundary is therefore required. It must preserve capability authority, BrowserContext/Page isolation, lifecycle cleanup, deadlines, cancellation and browser availability while remaining replaceable and engine-neutral above the provider adapter.

Goals.Goal: Supersede the predecessor only to correct ObservedWriteScope for the three authorized files.
Define an experimental engine-neutral request-policy/interception contract for bounded pre-dispatch network request decisions.
Wire the real CEF provider so an eligible request can be paused only for a bounded decision interval and then explicitly allowed or blocked.
Keep adblock, privacy and future request-policy semantics outside the kernel and outside the CEF adapter.
Implement one ordinary replaceable adblock policy plugin as the first proving consumer using only the minimal deterministic rule model required for acceptance evidence.
Prove on loopback infrastructure that a blocked request never reaches the origin server while an allowed request does reach it.
Prove that timeout, crash, unload or restart of the optional adblock policy cannot deadlock or terminate ordinary browser navigation.
Measure the incremental latency and concurrency behavior of the real interception path before committing to a long-term hot-path execution strategy.
Preserve the ability to replace the minimal proving blocker later with a provider that reuses an established filtering engine or compatible rule format without changing kernel or CEF product policy.

Constraints.Constraint: No functional, architectural, acceptance, task, verification, graph, or apply semantics may change in this correction.
SPEC APPROVAL AND EXACT PLAN APPROVAL REMAIN SEPARATE; THIS DRAFT DOES NOT AUTHORIZE IMPLEMENTATION.
C-BROWSER-DOWNLOADS-COOKIES-REALITY-REMEDIATION-20260901 MUST REMAIN APPLIED AND ARCHIVED BEFORE THIS CHANGE'S PLAN IS APPROVED OR EXECUTED.
REQUEST POLICY AND ADBLOCK ARE ORDINARY REPLACEABLE PLUGIN CAPABILITIES. NO ADBLOCK RULE, TRACKER LIST, HOST PATTERN OR BROWSER PRODUCT POLICY MAY ENTER THE KERNEL.
THE CEF PROVIDER MAY IMPLEMENT ONLY THE ENGINE MECHANISM REQUIRED TO PAUSE, RESUME OR CANCEL A REQUEST AND TO MARSHAL ENGINE-NEUTRAL METADATA. IT MUST NOT CONTAIN ADBLOCK-SPECIFIC RULE EVALUATION.

IF THE CURRENT CAPABILITY RPC MECHANISM CAN SATISFY THE REQUIRED BOUNDED SYNCHRONOUS INTERCEPTION SEMANTICS WITHOUT REENTRANCY OR DEADLOCK HAZARDS, IT MAY BE REUSED. OTHERWISE ANY NEW KERNEL MECHANISM MUST BE GENERIC INTERCEPTION INFRASTRUCTURE, NOT A BROWSER-SPECIFIC OR ADBLOCK-SPECIFIC PRIVILEGED PATH.
STABLE Browser Contract v1.0 WIRE FORMS AND EXISTING EXPERIMENTAL 0.1/0.2 BROWSER ENGINE PRIMITIVES MUST NOT BE INCOMPATIBLY REDEFINED IN PLACE.
NEW REQUEST-POLICY CONTRACTS START EXPERIMENTAL AND MUST NOT CLAIM V1 STABILITY IN THIS CHANGE.

REQUEST METADATA EXPOSED TO POLICY MUST BE MINIMAL. RAW COOKIE VALUES, AUTHORIZATION HEADERS, CLIENT CERTIFICATE MATERIAL, REQUEST BODIES, UPLOAD BYTES AND ARBITRARY RESPONSE CONTENT ARE NOT EXPOSED BY DEFAULT.

FULL REQUEST URL MAY BE EXPOSED ONLY TO AN AUTHORIZED POLICY PRINCIPAL FOR THE ADMITTED BrowserContextId/PageId SCOPE BECAUSE FILTERING REQUIRES URL-LEVEL MATCHING; GENERIC EVENTS AND METRICS MUST NOT ECHO SENSITIVE QUERY CONTENT BY DEFAULT.
POSSESSION OF BrowserContextId, PageId, URL OR A POLICY RULE ID ALONE MUST NOT CONFER INTERCEPTION AUTHORITY.
POLICY OBSERVATION AUTHORITY AND POLICY DECISION/INTERCEPTION AUTHORITY ARE DISTINCT. A PRINCIPAL ALLOWED TO OBSERVE REQUEST METADATA MUST NOT AUTOMATICALLY GAIN THE ABILITY TO BLOCK REQUESTS.
REQUEST-POLICY AUTHORITY IS SCOPED TO THE TARGET BROWSER CONTEXT AND, WHERE APPLICABLE, PAGE. A POLICY ADMITTED FOR CONTEXT A MUST NOT INSPECT OR CONTROL REQUESTS FROM CONTEXT B.
EVERY INTERCEPTION HAS A FINITE DEADLINE. NO POLICY PLUGIN MAY HOLD A CEF NETWORK CALLBACK, IO THREAD OR WORLDLINE PROVIDER INDEFINITELY.

THE FIRST ADBLOCK CONSUMER IS OPTIONAL AND FAILS OPEN: TIMEOUT, CRASH, UNLOAD, QUARANTINE OR UNAVAILABLE POLICY ALLOWS ORDINARY BROWSING TO CONTINUE AND PRODUCES A BOUNDED DIAGNOSTIC FACT. SECURITY-CRITICAL FAIL-CLOSED NETWORK POLICY IS OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS CHANGE.
INTERCEPTION CALLBACKS AND THEIR LIVE HANDLES BELONG TO A LIFECYCLE SCOPE AND ARE REMOVED OR INVALIDATED ON PLUGIN UNLOAD, CRASH OR REPLACEMENT.
THE NETWORK HOT PATH MUST NOT ACQUIRE AN UNBOUNDED GLOBAL LOCK, WAIT ON AN UNBOUNDED MAILBOX OR PERFORM UNBOUNDED RULE PARSING PER REQUEST.

THE PLAN MUST INCLUDE A REAL-PROVIDER LATENCY/CONCURRENCY SPIKE BEFORE FREEZING THE HOT-PATH EXECUTION STRATEGY. IF ACCEPTABLE PERFORMANCE REQUIRES EMBEDDING ADBLOCK-SPECIFIC POLICY IN CEF OR KERNEL, STOP AND REPLAN INSTEAD.
THE MINIMAL PROVING ADBLOCK RULE MODEL IS NOT A NEW WORLDLINE FILTER-LIST STANDARD. IT EXISTS ONLY TO PROVE THE INTERCEPTION BOUNDARY.
PUBLIC INTERNET ACCESS IS NOT REQUIRED FOR ACCEPTANCE. ALL REQUEST-POLICY NETWORK PROVING USES DETERMINISTIC LOOPBACK OR REPOSITORY-OWNED FIXTURES.
EXISTING M0, M1.1, M1.2, TABS/HISTORY, DOWNLOADS/COOKIES AND REAL-S3B ACCEPTANCE GATES ARE NOT WEAKENED, SKIPPED OR REPLACED TO MAKE THIS CHANGE GREEN.

WINDOWS-FIRST CEF IMPLEMENTATION REMAINS BEHIND PLATFORM-NEUTRAL CONTRACTS. NON-WINDOWS WORKSPACE COMPILATION MUST REMAIN GREEN AND UNSUPPORTED REAL CEF PATHS MUST FAIL EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN THROUGH MISSING IMPORTS OR PLATFORM TYPE LEAKAGE.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Do not add behavior, refactor implementation, weaken tests, or modify graph/verification projections in this scope correction.
Building a full new competitor to uBlock Origin, AdGuard or similar blockers.
Inventing a permanent Worldline-specific filter-list language.
Full EasyList, uBO, AdGuard or ABP syntax compatibility in this slice.
Cosmetic filtering or DOM element hiding.
Redirect or upgrade rules beyond what is strictly required for proving allow/block semantics.
Malware reputation, safe-browsing or antivirus policy.
Enterprise or parental fail-closed policy semantics.
Final adblock settings or shell UI.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The replacement plan is identical in functional scope to the predecessor and adds only the three authorized files to ObservedWriteScope.

docs/adr/ADR-BROWSER-SERVICE-PLUGINS-V1.md is updated or a bounded request policy companion ADR is added to document interception semantics, authority, failure behavior, lifecycle ownership and the hot-path design without reopening unrelated accepted M1.3 service architecture.

An engine-neutral experimental request metadata DTO exists and includes only fields justified by filtering, covering at least BrowserContextId, PageId where known, request URL, HTTP method, resource type and initiator or top-level origin where the engine can provide it reliably.
The contract defines an explicit pre-dispatch decision with at least `Allow` and `Block` outcomes and a bounded decision deadline.
Request metadata and decision contracts contain no CEF objects, Chromium structs, HWND, raw engine pointers, provider-local filesystem paths or platform-specific handles.
Request-policy observation and interception use separate authority classes and the provider rejects a decision caller that lacks admitted authority for the exact BrowserContextId/PageId scope.
A policy principal authorized for BrowserContext A cannot observe or block requests issued by BrowserContext B, even when both contexts load the same loopback origin.
Existing stable Browser Contract v1.0 fixtures and existing experimental engine 0.1/0.2 fixtures remain compatible; any new primitive is additive or separately versioned.
The real CEF provider invokes the interception boundary before the target eligible network request is dispatched and honors `Allow` and `Block` without embedding adblock-specific policy.
CEF network or IO callbacks are never blocked without a finite timeout; timeout handling is deterministic and covered by acceptance evidence.
The optional adblock policy timeout, crash, unload or unavailable state resolves fail-open and ordinary navigation remains operational.
Plugin unload/restart removes stale interception registrations and no callback may target a dead RuntimeId or retain authority from a previous runtime generation.

A minimal ordinary adblock policy plugin exists as the first proving consumer. Its rule representation is explicitly marked fixture/reference quality rather than a permanent public Worldline filter syntax.
The proving adblock plugin can express deterministic host/URL matching sufficient to block one loopback subresource while allowing another.

A loopback origin records inbound requests. A real CEF acceptance proves an allowed deterministic subresource reaches the origin and a blocked deterministic subresource produces zero corresponding origin hits.
Blocking a subresource does not terminate the page, provider process, browser context, tabs/history/downloads/cookies services or unrelated requests.

A policy decision may produce a bounded post-outcome observation carrying safe metadata such as decision kind, policy provider identity and opaque rule identifier, but that event is not consulted to determine the request outcome.
Raw Authorization/Cookie header values, request bodies and upload bytes do not enter policy DTOs, ordinary request-policy events, generic metrics, panic text or Debug output in the proving path.

The real-provider spike records interception throughput and latency under a deterministic request set, including at least no-policy baseline and active-policy measurements, and reports the execution topology used for each measurement.

The plan names an explicit performance stop/replan condition based on the spike evidence before choosing any architecture that performs a cross-process policy round trip for every production subresource.

Static architecture checks prove `worldline-kernel` contains no adblock, tracker-list or browser request-policy domain types and `worldline-browser-cef` contains no adblock-specific rule engine or filter list implementation.
Static architecture checks prove request-policy/adblock service crates do not become dependencies of unrelated tabs, history, downloads or cookies services merely to preserve browsing functionality.

BrowserServices or a separately named request-policy CI suite covers contract compatibility, authority isolation, deadline behavior, lifecycle cleanup, fail-open failure isolation and deterministic policy evaluation.

A real hosted Windows request-policy proving path bootstraps the pinned CEF runtime, executes the native provider path and demonstrates allow/block semantics against loopback without using ReferenceBrowserBackend as the claimed production evidence.

Source, Correctness, ArchitectureSecurity, ProvingSlice, RealChromium, BrowserProvider, BrowserServices, Real-S3B and All remain green locally; any new hosted request-policy gate is additive and the final hosted master run is named separately.
After fresh evidence and explicit apply confirmation, GRACE may extend M-BROWSER-SERVICE-PLUGINS and its verification projection with the request-policy slice; M1.3 remains Active.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh evidence names the experimental request-policy contract revision, authority separation, cross-context isolation, real CEF pre-dispatch allow/block behavior, zero-hit proof for blocked loopback requests, lifecycle cleanup, fail-open timeout/crash behavior, hot-path latency and concurrency measurements, architecture guards, preserved existing browser service gates and a successful hosted master run. Local and hosted evidence are reported separately.

Assumptions.Assumption: The existing implementation and named evidence remain unchanged while the replacement plan is reviewed; final GRACE evidence may reuse fresh unchanged runs, with lifecycle lint rerun after approval.
The previously verified real CEF provider and Real-S3B path remain the production evidence baseline consumed by this change rather than being reopened as reference-only scaffolding.

CEF exposes a maintained interception callback suitable for pausing or cancelling eligible requests without requiring a Chromium fork. If this assumption is false, the change stops and records evidence before any Chromium fork or browser-specific kernel exception is introduced.

Existing capability admission, deadlines, cancellation and lifecycle ownership can either express this bounded interception safely or can be extended generically without browser-specific kernel policy.
Cosmetic filtering, scriptlets and other DOM/content policy can remain a separate follow-on slice after network interception is verified.
DevTools, search providers and crypto/trust compatibility remain separate M1.3 changes.
